clue.text: Get high on heroin. Injecting one mil makes body spasm

indicators.note: something injected goes into the body, so the next pieces are put inside the first
the word for getting high is placed on, after, the drug letter

parts.note: to get up is to rise, to get high
I is the Roman numeral for one
mil is a pharmacy abbreviation for a millilitre, which is one cubic centimetre, cc

explanation.surface: A grim drug-use scene: getting high by injecting heroin brings on convulsions.
explanation.walkthrough: The drug scene is a decoy: 'mil' is the pharmacy shorthand for a millilitre, which is the same volume as one cubic centimetre.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiccup is an involuntary spasm of the diaphragm, a small bodily convulsion.

clue.text: Image of Billy, his third after wedding vow

indicators.note: the third letter of Billy's name

explanation.surface: A photo of a man named Billy, apparently his third marriage portrait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts Billy's letter behind the vow. 'Third' reads as a third wedding, but it only picks a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol was first a carved image of a god, and still means any image or likeness that is revered.

clue.text: Linked thing about one English paper's leader

parts.note: a chain is a thing of links

explanation.surface: Someone describes a linked item carried about by the editor of an English newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paper's leader' looks like a phrase meaning editor; in fact the 's is 'is', and 'leader' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a clan is its chief, and a chieftain is simply a leader of a tribe or band.

clue.text: Beat yak with shortened device

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to tap rapidly, as rain beats on a roof
second meaning: glib, fast talk, as in a salesman's line

indicators.note: the word for a device is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a device is a decorative design or emblem, a pattern

explanation.surface: Someone thrashes a yak using a gadget that has been cut down.
explanation.walkthrough: Two meanings and a wordplay share one answer. 'Yak' looks like the animal, but here it is chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain patters when it beats lightly and fast, and a salesman's patter is his rapid chatter, the yak.

clue.text: Covered decking in preserver and a hardener

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the following words

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of 'preserver', through 'and a', into the start of 'hardener'

explanation.surface: Timber decking with a roof, treated with wood preservative and hardener.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a genuine DIY instruction for decking, so the definition sits right at home: VERANDAH runs from preserVER to Hardener.
explanation.definitionFit: A verandah is a roofed platform along the outside of a house, i.e. decking with a cover.

clue.text: University heads gambling, for example, on probability with second roll-over

indicators.note: with means alongside, so the reversed piece is added after the rest
in a down entry one piece on another sits above it, so the vice comes first

parts.note: gambling is an example of a vice, a bad habit

indicators.note: turned over, the letters read in reverse

parts.note: the word roll taken as written

explanation.surface: University bosses are betting, with a jackpot carried forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roll-over' suggests a lottery jackpot carried forward, but the hyphenated word splits into a piece and its reversal signal. Vice-chancellors run British universities day to day.
explanation.definitionFit: In British universities the vice-chancellor is the chief executive, the head in practice.

clue.text: The Listener follows programme on before show again

indicators.note: to follow is to come after

parts.note: an app is a computer program

explanation.surface: The Listener magazine's crossword appears after some programme, before a repeat showing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Listener is italicised as a publication (also a famous crossword series), but here it is simply the organ that listens.
explanation.definitionFit: To show is to appear, so showing again is reappearing, a plain synonym.

clue.text: No one wants a student around time of birth

indicators.note: needs, so the pieces sit together

parts.note: N for no, as on a Y/N form

explanation.surface: Nobody wants to have a student hanging around them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time of birth' looks like the definition, but 'time' belongs to the wordplay: the pieces from 'No one' and 'a student' wrap around its letter, leaving 'of birth'.
explanation.definitionFit: Natal is the adjective of birth, from Latin natus, born, as in prenatal and natal day.

clue.text: Charge copper getting appeal in lawsuit

indicators.note: 'in' means inside, so copper and appeal are placed inside the lawsuit

explanation.surface: A police officer being charged, with an appeal lodged in the lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' is a policeman on the surface, which suits 'charge' and 'lawsuit', but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: An accusation is a charge brought against someone.

clue.text: Considering everything, one wants to shuffle off this coil

indicators.note: the letters of THIS COIL are shuffled

explanation.surface: Hamlet's 'shuffle off this mortal coil': someone taking the long view longs for death.
explanation.walkthrough: The line quotes Hamlet's 'to be or not to be' speech, where shuffling off this mortal coil means dying; here 'shuffle' is taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Holistic means treating the whole rather than the parts.

clue.text: Whip round wearing floppy hat and tie

indicators.note: the floppy hat is worn around the next piece, which goes inside it
a floppy hat loses its shape, so the letters of hat are put out of order
turned round, the word reads backwards

parts.note: a cat, short for cat-o'-nine-tails, is a whip

explanation.surface: A person wearing a whip and a floppy hat, and tying something on.
explanation.walkthrough: The whip is a cat, short for cat-o'-nine-tails; the clue nods to Dr Seuss's Cat in the Hat, which is literally what the wordplay builds.
explanation.definitionFit: To attach one thing to another is to fasten or tie it on.

clue.text: Gloss over what Marie Curie's kids were

definitions.meaning: of a Polish mother and a French father

explanation.surface: Someone skates over the fact of what Marie Curie's children were.
explanation.walkthrough: Marie Curie was Polish-born and married the Frenchman Pierre Curie, so their daughters were French-Polish. 'Gloss over' reads as one phrase; split it.
explanation.definitionFit: French polish is a high-gloss shellac finish for wood.

clue.text: She was barely noticed riding for £5 in Hackney

definitions.meaning: the legendary naked ride through Coventry, when townsfolk kept their eyes shut
Cockney rhyming slang for a fiver

explanation.surface: A woman rode past almost unseen, for a five-pound fare in east London.
explanation.walkthrough: Legend says Lady Godiva rode naked through Coventry while townsfolk looked away. Hackney is a Cockney area of London, and in rhyming slang a 'Lady Godiva' is a fiver, a £5 note.
explanation.definitionFit: Godiva rode 'barely' clothed, and Lady Godiva rhymes with fiver.

clue.text: Ditch Harket initially seen fronting Norwegian group

indicators.note: the letter is placed in front, as a singer fronts a band
only the opening letter of Harket is taken

parts.note: Morten Harket, lead singer of a-ha; his name starts with H
a-ha is the Norwegian pop band known for 'Take On Me'

explanation.surface: Morten Harket is spotted as frontman of his Norwegian band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harket initially' gives H, 'seen fronting' puts it before A-HA; Harket really does front a-ha. A ha-ha is a sunken ditch with a wall on one side, used on English estates to keep livestock out unseen.
explanation.definitionFit: A ha-ha is a sunken ditch acting as a hidden boundary fence in landscaped grounds.

clue.text: A plant from Panorama ran that clip!

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the words that follow
a clip is a short extract cut from a longer piece, so the answer is a run of letters cut from the phrase

parts.note: the letters run on from the end of Panorama through ran into the start of that

explanation.surface: The BBC's current affairs show Panorama broadcast a clip about a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Panorama is a long-running BBC documentary programme; 'from' and 'clip' say a stretch is cut out of panorAMA RAN THat.
explanation.definitionFit: Amaranth is a flowering plant, grown both as an ornamental and for its edible grain.

clue.text: Understand fear Nick!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to grasp or comprehend
second meaning: to anticipate with dread
third meaning: to arrest, British slang for a police arrest

explanation.walkthrough: Three separate meanings of one word, strung together so they read like an excited command. In British slang to nick someone is to arrest them.
explanation.definitionFit: Apprehend covers grasping an idea, dreading something to come (as in apprehensive) and seizing a suspect.

clue.text: Labels are ones that don't twist

definitions.meaning: card players who stand pat in pontoon

explanation.surface: A definition of labels as things that don't twist.
explanation.walkthrough: In pontoon, the British card game like blackjack, a player may 'stick' (stand) or 'twist' (take another card); stickers are those who don't twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Stickers are labels with glue on the back; in pontoon those who stick rather than twist are also stickers.

clue.text: Happily, after vacation, presidential leader's no longer in charge! Entrancing thought!

indicators.note: once its insides are vacated, emptied out, only the first and last letters of happily remain

parts.note: with its middle vacated, only the outer letters H and Y are left

indicators.note: the leading, first letter of presidential

parts.note: no longer means not any more, so NOT

explanation.surface: Joy at the thought that the president is finally out of office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after vacation' sounds like a holiday but means the word is emptied of its middle, and 'no longer in charge' reads as one phrase but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypnotic means mesmerising, holding attention as if by a spell, so entrancing.

clue.text: Ring back and make a disdainful sound

indicators.note: 'back' means in the reverse direction, so the word is read from end to start

explanation.surface: Someone phones back and snorts dismissively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring back' reads as returning a phone call; the ring is a hoop.
explanation.definitionFit: To pooh is to say 'pooh!' in contempt.

clue.text: Cruise to the south of Cuba and America results in import tax

parts.note: C is Cuba's international vehicle code

explanation.surface: A cruise south of Cuba and the US lands passengers with import duties.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital C on 'Cruise' is hidden by its first-word position; it is Tom Cruise, not a voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: Custom (usually customs) is duty levied on imports.

clue.text: Garden study or hut I rebuilt, with reluctant worker dismissed

indicators.note: the letters are rearranged
ANT is removed from RELUCTANT

parts.note: RELUCTANT without ANT, the worker insect

explanation.surface: A garden study or rebuilt hut, now that the reluctant worker has been sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: The ant is crosswords' standard worker. What is left of 'reluctant' joins OR HUT I in the rebuild.
explanation.definitionFit: Horticulture is the study and practice of growing garden plants, from Latin hortus, garden.

clue.text: Time old and young get refill when only a bit drunk

definitions.text: refill when only a bit drunk

parts.note: a pup is a young animal

explanation.surface: Old and young alike get a refill when they've only had a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit drunk' suggests tipsy, but it means a glass only partly drunk from.
explanation.definitionFit: A top-up refills a glass that has only been partly emptied.

clue.text: Gets on when there's no time to get in

explanation.surface: A complaint about a queue: you grow old when there's no time to get in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets on' means grows older. 'Ages' also means a long time, which the surface plays against 'no time'.
explanation.definitionFit: To get on is an idiom for growing old, and to age is the plain verb for the same thing.

clue.text: Unconventional sort of dodgy finance contract written in hurry

indicators.note: a thing written in something is set inside it

parts.note: payment protection insurance, notoriously mis-sold by British banks

explanation.surface: A dodgy finance deal signed in a rush by someone unconventional.
explanation.walkthrough: PPI is payment protection insurance, whose mass mis-selling became a British banking scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: A hippie is someone who rejects conventional society.

clue.text: To be heavier than two huge bananas one's eaten

indicators.note: crazy, so the letters are scrambled
what is eaten ends up inside the eater, so I goes into the other letters

parts.note: one = I, eaten by the rest

explanation.surface: Someone who has eaten a banana weighs more than two huge ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like fruit to weigh, but it means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Outweigh is a plain synonym: to weigh out more than something else on the scales.

clue.text: His parts are rewritten for musicians

indicators.note: the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A composer's parts are rewritten to suit the players.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a composer arranging parts, which suits musicians so well the anagram hides in plain sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Harpists are musicians who play the harp.

clue.text: Fashionable second course

parts.note: a mo = a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A trendy second course at dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second course' reads as the main course of a meal; split it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mode is a fashion, and modish, 'in the mode', means fashionable: a plain synonym.
